newsitem.title: INDIA: India oil pipeline burst shuts down two refineries.
newsitem.headline: India oil pipeline burst shuts down two refineries.

text.p: Two major oil refineries were shut down on Thursday after an oil pipeline burst in India's northeastern state of Assam sparking off a seven-hour blaze, an oil company official said.
"The Bongaigaon refinery and the Barauni refinery have shut down operations today," M Bhandari, the chief engineer in charge of the pipelines of state-run Oil India Limited (OIL), told Reuters.
Bongaigaon Refineries and Petrochemicals Ltd, located in Assam, have an annual capacity of 1.35 million tonnes.
Barauni, in the nearby eastern state of Bihar, is owned by the Indian Oil Corp, the country's largest oil refiner. It has an annual processing capacity of 3.3 million tonnes.
Bhandari said operations at both refineries would probably be suspended for an indefinite period.
"The pumping of crude has been held up for an indefinite period," he said.
Bhandari said three pipelines, used to pump crude oil to Bongaigaon and Barauni refineries, had been damaged at Hajo, 30 km (19 miles) from the state capital of Guwahati.
Two pipelines belonged to OIL and one to IOC, he added.
Firemen battled for seven hours before the blaze could be put out.
"We have put out the fire and stopped the crude outflow," he said. "The area has been cordoned off by the army and police."
Bhandari said two explosions before the fire broke out led him to believe that separatist insurgents had triggered the pipeline burst and the ensuing fire.
"Today morning between 5 and 5.30 (2330 GMT and 0000 GMT), two bombs went off at Hajo 30 km (19 miles) northwest of Guwahati," Bhandari said.

He said he suspected the bombs were planted there by the separatist militants. Several separatist militant groups are fighting for separate homeland or independence in the remote northeastern state of Assam.
